title: The Parish of the Fens Again
premise: Kestrel Coldharbour, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired to finalize a payout on Maren Dusk, a fenland parish organist who vanished three years ago and was legally declared dead. When Kestrel discovers Maren's diary in a flooded chapel, its entries continue past the disappearance date — written in Maren's hand but describing events Kestrel is living in real time. As Kestrel follows the diary's prophecies through the parish's tangled loyalties, they uncover that Maren faked her death to escape a controlling family and a forbidden love, and that the diary is being continued now by someone who knew her intimately. The trail ends in the drained fen at the parish's edge, where Kestrel confronts the diarist — Maren herself, alive and watching — and must choose between exposing her to honor the truth and duty of their profession, or letting her vanish again out of love for the person she was trying to become.
about_author: Jonah Okafor is the pen name of a former rural claims adjuster who spent a decade walking the waterlogged byways of eastern England and never stopped wondering about the cases that closed too neatly. The Parish of the Fens Again is the second novel to feature investigator Kestrel Coldharbour.

chapters.title: The Claim That Wouldn't Dry
chapters.summary: Kestrel Coldharbour's POV. Kestrel arrives in the fen parish of Saltmere to close the Dusk life-insurance claim, annoyed by its three-year staleness. A tour of the drowned chapel reveals Maren's diary hidden in the organ bench — and its final entry is dated last week. The emotional beat is professional detachment cracking into unease.

chapters.title: Ink Under Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Forensic tests prove the late entries are written in period ink, not modern forgery, and the handwriting matches Maren's perfectly. Kestrel interviews the vicar and Maren's brother Aldous, both brittle with rehearsed grief. Beat: the first diary entry describes Kestrel's own arrival, word for word.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with an interlude from the anonymous diarist. Kestrel pulls the old police file and finds the disappearance ruled a drowning on thin evidence — and notices the investigating officer now works for the Dusk family's business. Beat: the thrill of a reopened hunt shadowed by the diary predicting each of Kestrel's moves.

chapters.title: The Organist's Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV alternates between Kestrel and Elowen, a young choir member who was Maren's secret protégée. Elowen reveals Maren had a lover the family forbade — someone still in the parish. Kestrel realizes the diary's newest pages describe conversations Elowen and Kestrel had yesterday. Beat: intimacy and dread braided together.

chapters.title: What the Fen Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following a diary clue to a drainage sluice, Kestrel is nearly drowned in a staged 'accident' — the parish's third in three years. Photographic memory of the water marks proves it was murder attempted, not mischance. Beat: fear hardening into fury; Kestrel is now inside the case, not beside it.

chapters.title: Aldous Dusk's Perfect Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel uncovers that Aldous has been forging Maren's signature on documents for years to control her inheritance, and that the 'closed' case protected him. The diary's next page predicts Aldous will destroy the organ tonight — and he does. Beat: the sickening confirmation that the diarist sees everything Kestrel sees.

chapters.title: The Hand That Writes Me
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, spiraling toward obsession. Comparing diary pages photographically, Kestrel finds the recent entries were written left-handed by someone concealing their identity — and spots a detail only a lover would know: the nickname Maren used for the person she fled to. Beat: grief for Maren reframed as the possibility she is alive.

chapters.title: Vespers for the Missing
chapters.summary: Elowen's POV. During a parish service, Elowen recognizes the organ style of the anonymous visiting organist as Maren's own — a style she alone taught no one. She says nothing, torn between loyalty to Maren's secret and truth owed to Kestrel. Beat: the theme of loyalty versus truth made flesh in a single held note.

chapters.title: The Drained Fen
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the diary's final unfinished sentence to a keeper's cottage on the newly drained fen, Kestrel comes face to face with Maren Dusk — alive, writing the diary to draw out whoever tried to kill her, which she believed was Kestrel's client. Aldous arrives to finish what he started. Beat: the climax, where love, duty, and truth collide in the mud and reeds.

chapters.title: Again, the Parish of the Fens
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing with Maren's. Aldous confesses under the weight of Kestrel's memory-evidence; Maren chooses to testify rather than vanish, surrendering her new identity to save Elowen from suspicion. Kestrel files a report that tells the truth and asks for nothing — and mails Maren a blank diary. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity chosen, not assigned.
